page.h1: HTS Chapter 12: Oil Seeds and Oleaginous Fruits; Miscellaneous Grains, Seeds and Fruit; Industrial or Medicinal Plants; Straw and Fodder — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Chapter 12 Export Markets: Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Soybeans & Oilseeds
seo.shortDescription: What China, Mexico, the EU, Japan and other buyers charge on U.S. Chapter 12 exports, by product group.

intro: For almost every market in this chapter, access is decided by import demand and crushing capacity, not by a tariff — Mexico, Canada, the EU, Japan and Egypt all buy this chapter's goods duty-free. China is the one exception: it still charges the 10% extra tariff from the 2025 U.S.–China tariff fight on top of its normal rate, and its own 2018–19 retaliation tariff, though waived for soybeans through an exclusion process, remains on the books.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

assumptions: Rates come from each market's own 2026 tariff schedule (EU Combined Nomenclature, Japan's Statistical Code for Import, Mexico's TIGIE, Canada's Customs Tariff, China's Customs Tariff) or, for Egypt, Indonesia and Pakistan, the best available secondary reporting where the official schedule could not be confirmed — flagged above as unconfirmed.

One subheading (1201.90, non-seed soybeans) stands in for each market's whole-chapter rate; a few markets charge a different rate on seed soybeans (1201.10) or on the chapter's smaller headings, which this page averages rather than lists individually.
Trade agreement rates apply only to goods that meet the agreement's rule of origin; China's 10% reciprocal tariff and its separate, soybean-specific exclusion process are explained on Tariff updates.
National 8–10-digit tariff lines can set a different rate than the 6-digit HS subheading shown here — check the market's own schedule before relying on this page for a transaction.
